message.content:
**Short answer:**  
Yes – you can file a noise‑complaint in Atlanta, but the “local council” (the City Council) isn’t the first place to go. Noise complaints are handled by the city’s **Police Department** and the **Department of Public Safety / Code Enforcement**. The City Council can help if the issue isn’t resolved, but the initial filing goes to the police or the city’s online complaint system.

---

## How to File a Noise Complaint in Atlanta

| Step | What to Do | Where/How |
|------|------------|-----------|
| 1 | **Call 311** (Atlanta’s non‑emergency city services line) | 404‑656‑3111 (or dial 311 from any Atlanta phone) |
| 2 | **Use the online portal** | Visit the City of Atlanta’s official website: <https://www.atlantaga.gov> → “311” → “Noise Complaint” |
| 3 | **Email** | Send a detailed description to: <noisecomplaints@atlantaga.gov> |
| 4 | **Visit in person** | Go to the nearest Police Station or the City Hall’s Public Safety office. |

### Online Filing (recommended)

1. Go to <https://www.atlantaga.gov/311> (or search “Atlanta noise complaint” on the site).  
2. Select **“Noise Complaint”** from the list of services.  
3. Fill out the form with:
   * Your name & contact info  
   * Address or location of the noise source  
   * Time(s) and duration of the disturbance  
   * Description of the noise (e.g., loud music, construction, barking dogs)  
   * Any prior attempts to resolve the issue  
4. Submit. You’ll receive a confirmation number and an estimated response time.

### Phone Filing

- **Atlanta Police Department (Non‑Emergency)**: 404‑656‑3111  
- **Atlanta Police Department (Emergency)**: 911 (only if the noise is part of an emergency)

When you call, let the dispatcher know it’s a noise complaint and provide the same details you’d give on the online form.

---

## What Happens After You File

1. **Police Dispatch**: Officers will investigate the complaint.  
2. **Code Enforcement**: If the noise violates city ordinances (e.g., construction after 10 p.m., loud music after 11 p.m.), the Code Enforcement team may issue a citation or require corrective action.  
3. **Follow‑up**: You’ll receive a case number. If the issue isn’t resolved, you can request a status update by calling 311 or emailing the complaint address.

---

## Relevant Atlanta Noise Ordinance (Key Points)

| Section | What It Covers | Typical Hours |
|---------|----------------|---------------|
| **Construction** | Noise from building work | 7 a.m.–10 p.m. (no work after 10 p.m.) |
| **Music & Entertainment** | Loud music, amplified sound | 7 a.m.–11 p.m. (no loud music after 11 p.m.) |
| **Pets** | Excessive barking | 7 a.m.–11 p.m. (no barking after 11 p.m.) |
| **General** | Any other noise that disturbs the peace | 7 a.m.–11 p.m. (no disturbances after 11 p.m.) |

*(These are simplified summaries; the full ordinance is available on the City of Atlanta website.)*

---

## If the Issue Persists

- **Contact the City Council**: If the police or Code Enforcement don’t resolve the problem, you can bring it to the attention of your local council member.  
  - Find your council member: <https://www.atlantaga.gov/council>  
  - Email or call their office to request a meeting or intervention.

- **File a Formal Complaint**: The City Council can file a formal complaint with the city’s administrative offices, which may prompt a more thorough investigation.

---

### Quick Reference Links

| Resource | Link |
|----------|------|
| City of Atlanta 311 | <https://www.atlantaga.gov/311> |
| Noise Complaint Form | <https://www.atlantaga.gov/311/noise> |
| Atlanta Police Department | <https://www.atlantapd.org> |
| City Code Enforcement | <https://www.atlantaga.gov/code-enforcement> |
| City Council Contact | <https://www.atlantaga.gov/council> |

---

**Bottom line:** Yes, you can report a noise complaint in Atlanta. Use the 311 system, the online portal, or call the police. The City Council can help if the problem isn’t resolved through the usual channels.
